title: New Governor, Old Problem: Koja Confronts US Base-Related Crimes in Okinawa
author: Charmaine N. Willis
text:
Okinawa Governor Koja Genta (left) lodges a written protest over the murder of a woman, allegedly by a U.S. Marine, with Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae (center) and Chief Cabinet Secretary Kihara Minou, Oct. 7, 2026.
Credit: Facebook/ Koja Genta
Okinawa’s September 2026 election made headlines as incumbent Denny Tamaki was ousted by the Liberal Democratic Party’s (LDP) preferred candidate, Koja Genta. Koja became the first LDP-backed candidate to win the position since Hirokazu Nakaima in 2006. Tamaki and his predecessor, the late Onaga Takeshi, vocally opposed the expansion of the U.S. Marine Corps’ Camp Schwab in Henoko and were generally critical of Okinawa’s excessive base burden, relative to other Japanese prefectures. Newly-elected Governor Koja was perceived by the LDP-led Japanese government to be more favorable to the U.S. bases in Okinawa, specifically the completion of the relocation of Marine Corps Air Station Futenma in Ginowan City to Camp Schwab. [...]
